central_topic: Reliability and efficiency of heteroscedastic split-conformal regions for observed positive continuous compositions, using fixed isometric-logratio coordinates and training-only local-scale selection under IID and covariate-shift synthetic regimes.
core_methods: Split conformal with finite-sample order-statistic calibration and maximum standardized ILR residual scores
Fixed Helmert isometric-logratio representation with polynomial-ridge centers and log-residual base scales
Training-only cross-fitted residual-moment Gaussian-kernel smoothing with bounded shrink-to-neutral scalar scale corrections
Nested training-only swapped pseudo-calibration/evaluation splits selecting scales by conformal-rank ILR-box volume, with Gaussian-loss fallback
comparators: Unscaled maximum-ILR-residual split-conformal regions sharing fitted centers
Simplex-coordinate L-infinity split-conformal regions sharing fitted centers
Bonferroni per-coordinate conformal intervals for simultaneous compositional coverage
Training-only constant-center and whole-simplex reference predictors
Weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift as a literature comparator only, not an evaluated method
benchmarks: Synthetic composition-v1: logistic-normal IID, heteroscedastic Dirichlet IID, and Dirichlet covariate-shift cases, each at K=3 and K=8 with six covariates
Completed final evaluation: eight statistical seeds, train/calibration/test sizes 1024/512/2048 per case, alpha=0.05/0.10/0.20
Feature-defined subgroup audits and normalized simplex-volume estimates using 128 contexts and 1024 shared uniform-simplex probes
architectural_shifts: No neural architecture or coordinate-representation transition is evidenced. The strongest scale-only variants preserve polynomial-ridge centers, fixed Helmert ILR coordinates, and the region family; the supported procedural transition is from Gaussian-loss scale selection to training-only conformal-rank ILR-box-volume selection.
result_driven_themes: The rank-selected scale variant has the highest recorded search utility and a completed eight-seed final evaluation, but final evaluation of that variant alone does not establish a replicated selector-only causal advantage.

Final mean absolute coverage error is 0.013562011718750005 for IID cases versus 0.13034261067708333 for shifted cases; marginal calibration must not be advertised as conditional or covariate-shift validity.

Final aggregate utility exceeds the strongest aggregate comparator by 0.011594669497844157, yet mean simplex volume is 0.3034934467739529 versus 0.29170094596015084 for simplex L-infinity; there is no uniform volume-superiority claim.
ILR-box volume used for training selection and uniform-simplex reference volume used for evaluation are different measures under a nonlinear inverse transform.

Subgroup coverage, paired seed-block uncertainty, simultaneous baseline comparisons, and Monte Carlo resolution qualify efficiency and reliability conclusions; contexts and shared probes are not independent replicates.

queries.query: Tibshirani Barber Candes Ramdas Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift

queries.query: conformal prediction marginal coverage conditional coverage limitations
queries.rationale: The artifacts report two feature-defined subgroup coverages but implement pooled calibration. Literature on marginal versus conditional validity prevents subgroup diagnostics from being mistaken for conditional guarantees or evaluated Mondrian methods.

queries.query: logratio inverse transformation simplex Jacobian volume measure
queries.rationale: Training minimizes an ILR-box-volume surrogate, whereas evaluation integrates membership against uniform-simplex probes. Change-of-variables background explains why efficiency in one measure need not imply smallest simplex volume; this is not evidence that the surrogate caused any observed result.
